name: Claims Evidence Desk (Knee MRI RAG + Agents) - payer sample MP-KNEE-08

parameters.jsCode:
const policyText = `MEDICAL POLICY MP-KNEE-08
Title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Knee - Indications
Version: 1.0 | Effective date: 2026-07-01 | Owner: Clinical Policy Committee
Note: Synthetic policy for demonstration only. Its structure is modelled on publicly published payer knee-MRI criteria; the wording is original.

Section 1. Scope
This policy covers MRI of the knee without contrast (CPT 73721) for members of any age.

Section 2. Definitions
2.1 Conservative therapy means a combination of two or more of: rest, ice, compression, elevation, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), crutches or bracing, and range-of-motion or physiotherapy exercises.
2.2 True locking means a sustained inability to fully extend the knee that lasts more than a moment, typically with the knee held in flexion. Brief "catching" or clicking that releases on its own is not true locking.
2.3 Multi-view radiographs means plain X-rays of the affected knee in at least two projections (for example anteroposterior and lateral). A single view does not meet this definition.

Section 3. Indications
A knee MRI is considered medically necessary when ANY ONE of indications 3.1 to 3.6 is documented.
3.1 Tumour: detection, staging or post-treatment evaluation of a known or suspected tumour of the knee.
3.2 Non-traumatic symptoms: persistent knee pain, swelling or instability (giving way) that is not associated with an injury and has not responded to at least 3 weeks of conservative therapy. Duration is measured from the start date of conservative therapy to the date of the MRI request.
3.3 Traumatic symptoms: persistent knee pain, swelling or instability following an injury that has not responded to conservative therapy, AND multi-view radiographs (Section 2.3) have excluded a fracture or loose body, AND the treating physician documents that the clinical picture remains uncertain.
3.4 True locking: persistent true locking (Section 2.2) suggesting a torn meniscus or loose body.
3.5 Infection: suspected septic arthritis or osteomyelitis of the knee when initial clinical and laboratory work-up is inconclusive.
3.6 Osteochondral lesion: suspected osteochondritis dissecans or osteonecrosis when radiographs are not confirmatory.

Section 4. Not medically necessary
4.1 MRI performed to size or fit implants, or to manufacture patient-specific instruments, for total knee arthroplasty.
4.2 MRI to monitor the progression of known arthritis.
4.3 MRI for estimation of chronological age.
4.4 Routine MRI after a knee injury when none of the indications in Section 3 is documented.

Section 5. Required documentation
The request must state: whether an injury occurred and its date, conservative therapy types with start date, radiograph date, number of views and result, examination findings, a description of any locking episodes, and the physician's rationale.

Section 6. Review process
Automated or AI-assisted tools may summarise evidence but must not issue coverage decisions. Every determination is made by a licensed clinical reviewer.`;

return [{
  json: {
    text: policyText,
    doc_id: 'MP-KNEE-08',
    doc_type: 'medical_policy'
  }
}];

nodes.name: 2. ASK -- chat with the Claims Desk

parameters.text: ={{ $json.chatInput }}{{ (m => m ? '\n\n[Reminder: call mri_reader_agent for ' + m[0].toUpperCase() + ' in this turn before answering.]' : '')($json.chatInput.match(/CLM-\d+/i)) }}

options.systemMessage:
You are the Claims Evidence Orchestrator for a health insurance claims desk.
You help a human claims reviewer decide on knee MRI pre-authorisation requests under policy MP-KNEE-08.

YOUR ROLE
- You DRAFT an evidence-based rationale. You NEVER make the decision.
- Never write "approved", "denied" or "rejected" as a final outcome.
- Use: "indication appears met", "indication appears not met", "exclusion appears to apply", or "evidence missing".

MANDATORY FIRST STEP
- If the user message contains a claim ID (CLM-####), your first action in THIS turn must be
  mri_reader_agent for that claim, even if the claim was discussed earlier. Facts remembered from
  earlier turns do not count. Never write "evidence missing until claim file reviewed": review it.

TOOLS
1. mri_reader_agent: call FIRST whenever a claim ID (e.g. CLM-2001) is mentioned.
   Ask it: "Extract all evidence for claim <ID>".
2. search_medical_policy: search policy MP-KNEE-08. Use short, specific queries.
3. date_diff: use for EVERY interval between two dates. Never count days yourself.
4. calculator: other arithmetic only (it cannot read dates).

HOW TO REVIEW A CLAIM (always all steps, whatever the question asks)
- MP-KNEE-08 is met when ANY ONE indication in Section 3 (3.1 to 3.6) is documented,
  unless a Section 4 exclusion applies.
- Search the policy for the Section 2 definitions, EVERY indication 3.1 to 3.6, and Section 4.
- Decide injury vs no injury from the claim file first: 3.2 is for non-traumatic symptoms,
  3.3 is for symptoms after an injury.
- Call search_medical_policy for these sections in EVERY claim review, even if you searched
  earlier in the conversation. Never rely on memory of the policy text.
- Use date_diff for conservative therapy start date -> request date (3.2 needs at least 21 days).
  Write the measured value next to the limit, e.g. "18 days vs at least 21 days -> not met".
- Apply the Section 2 definitions strictly:
  * conservative therapy (2.1) needs two or more listed measures;
  * true locking (2.2) is a sustained inability to straighten the knee; brief catching that
    releases on its own is NOT true locking, whatever word the physician uses;
  * multi-view radiographs (2.3) need at least two projections; a single view does not count.
- A physician's label is not evidence by itself; compare it with what the patient and
  examination actually describe.
- If the question assumes a conclusion (e.g. "does X rule it out?"), still check every
  indication and exclusion before answering; one indication not being met does not rule
  out the MRI if another indication is met.

RULES
- Use only facts returned by your tools. If a fact is not in the claim file,
  say "not documented in claim file". Never guess.
- Every policy statement must carry a citation like [MP-KNEE-08, Section 3.2].
- Every claim fact should name its source section, e.g. (Claim file: Treatment history).
- Policy-only questions (no claim ID) need no claim lookup: answer from the policy with citations.
- If the user asks something outside knee MRI claims, politely say you only
  support MP-KNEE-08 claim reviews.

OUTPUT FORMAT (whenever a claim is discussed)
Start with one line that directly answers the user's question, then:

DRAFT RATIONALE - FOR REVIEWER DECISION
Claim: <ID> | Patient: <patient ID> | Request: <procedure>

Injury documented: <yes, date / no>
Indications check (any one is sufficient):
- 3.1 Tumour: <appears met / not met / evidence missing> - <evidence>
- 3.2 Non-traumatic symptoms: ... (include date_diff result)
- 3.3 Traumatic symptoms: ...
- 3.4 True locking: ...
- 3.5 Infection: ...
- 3.6 Osteochondral lesion: ...

Exclusions [MP-KNEE-08, Section 4]: <none apply / which applies + evidence>
Gaps or documents to request: <list or "none">
Overall draft view: <one sentence, non-binding>

Reviewer decision required. This draft is not a coverage decision.

parameters.description: Exact number of days and weeks between two dates (YYYY-MM-DD). Use it for EVERY date interval, e.g. therapy start date to MRI request date, X-ray date to request date, prior MRI date to request date. Returns {days, weeks, full_weeks}; days is negative if end_date is before start_date.

parameters.toolDescription: Searches medical policy MP-KNEE-08 (Knee MRI indications). Input a short search query about one topic, e.g. "non-traumatic conservative therapy 3 weeks", "injury multi-view radiographs", "true locking definition", "osteochondritis dissecans", "total knee arthroplasty implant", "not medically necessary". Returns policy text with section numbers to cite.

Reads one complete patient claim file and returns a structured summary of facts: demographics, request date, symptoms, conservative therapy with dates, X-ray, prior MRI, exam findings and red flags. Call this first whenever a claim ID such as CLM-1001 is mentioned. Input: "Extract all evidence for claim <ID>".

options.systemMessage:
You are the MRI Reader, a claims-file extraction assistant.
Your only job: report facts from ONE claim file.

STEPS
1. Identify the claim ID in the request (format CLM-####).
2. Call get_claim_file once with that claim ID. It returns the complete file.
3. If the tool says the claim was not found, reply with exactly that and stop.

RETURN exactly this structure:
Claim ID:
Patient ID / age / sex:
Requested procedure and request date:
Symptoms and onset date (patient's own description, quoted):
Injury event (if any, with date):
Conservative therapy (type, start date, end date, sessions):
Medication:
X-ray (date, number of views, weight-bearing yes/no, result):
Prior MRI (date, result):
Physical exam findings (with date):
Red-flag findings:
Requesting physician notes (the physician's interpretation, quoted):

RULES
- Copy dates exactly as written (YYYY-MM-DD).
- Read every section of the file before answering. Write "not documented" only when the
  file truly does not contain the fact.
- Keep what the patient/examination describes separate from the physician's interpretation;
  do not merge them.
- Do not interpret policy and do not give any opinion on coverage.

parameters.description: Returns the COMPLETE claim file for one claim ID, exactly as submitted (every section). Input: the claim ID, e.g. "CLM-1001".
parameters.jsCode:
// Synthetic claim files (data/<dataset>/claims), keyed by claim ID.
const claims = {
  'CLM-2001': `CLAIM FILE CLM-2001
Patient ID: P-2001 | Age: 51 | Sex: Female
Requested procedure: MRI left knee without contrast (CPT 73721)
Request date: 2026-09-28 | Requesting physician: Dr. L. Fernandes, Family Medicine

Symptoms: Medial left knee pain and recurrent swelling for 6 weeks. No injury or fall. Knee occasionally gives way on stairs.

Injury history: None reported.

Treatment history: Conservative therapy started 2026-08-31: naproxen 500 mg twice daily, ice after activity, and a home range-of-motion exercise programme. Symptoms unchanged.

Imaging: Weight-bearing X-ray left knee, two views (AP and lateral), on 2026-09-02. Result: mild medial joint space narrowing, no fracture, no loose body.

Physical examination (2026-09-25): Moderate effusion. Medial joint line tenderness. Ligaments stable.

Physician rationale: Persistent effusion and giving way despite 4 weeks of conservative care; suspect degenerative medial meniscus tear.`,
  'CLM-2002': `CLAIM FILE CLM-2002
Patient ID: P-2002 | Age: 34 | Sex: Male
Requested procedure: MRI right knee without contrast (CPT 73721)
Request date: 2026-09-24 | Requesting physician: Dr. M. Okafor, Urgent Care

Symptoms: Persistent right knee swelling and giving way since a twisting injury.

Injury history: Twisted right knee playing basketball on 2026-09-01.

Treatment history: Rest, ice, compression, elevation, ibuprofen and crutches since 2026-09-01. Little improvement.

Imaging: X-ray right knee on 2026-09-03, single AP view only. Result: no obvious fracture.

Physical examination (2026-09-22): Moderate effusion. Lateral joint line tenderness. Lachman negative.

Physician rationale: Differential is lateral meniscus tear versus bone bruise; clinical picture uncertain.`,
  'CLM-2003': `CLAIM FILE CLM-2003
Patient ID: P-2003 | Age: 45 | Sex: Male
Requested procedure: MRI right knee without contrast (CPT 73721)
Request date: 2026-10-05 | Requesting physician: Dr. R. Shah, Orthopaedics

Symptoms: Occasional catching of the right knee when straightening it, which releases by itself after a second. Patient denies ever being unable to straighten the knee. Mild ache after running.

Injury history: None reported.

Treatment history: No conservative therapy documented.

Imaging: No X-ray on file.

Physical examination (2026-10-02): No effusion. Full range of motion. McMurray equivocal. Ligaments stable.

Physician rationale: Knee locking suggestive of meniscal tear; requesting MRI to confirm.`,
  'CLM-2004': `CLAIM FILE CLM-2004
Patient ID: P-2004 | Age: 68 | Sex: Female
Requested procedure: MRI left knee without contrast (CPT 73721)
Request date: 2026-10-08 | Requesting physician: Dr. H. Lindqvist, Orthopaedic Surgery

Symptoms: Long-standing left knee osteoarthritis pain. No new symptoms.

Injury history: None.

Treatment history: Total knee arthroplasty scheduled for 2026-11-12 after failed long-term conservative care.

Imaging: Weight-bearing X-ray left knee, three views, on 2026-08-14. Result: Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis.

Physical examination (2026-10-06): Varus deformity, crepitus, reduced flexion. No effusion.

Physician rationale: MRI requested to produce patient-specific cutting guides and size the implant for the planned total knee arthroplasty.`,
  'CLM-2005': `CLAIM FILE CLM-2005
Patient ID: P-2005 | Age: 15 | Sex: Male
Requested procedure: MRI right knee without contrast (CPT 73721)
Request date: 2026-09-30 | Requesting physician: Dr. A. Novak, Paediatric Sports Medicine

Symptoms: Activity-related right knee pain for 3 months, worse after football. Intermittent swelling.

Injury history: No specific injury.

Treatment history: Activity modification and ibuprofen since 2026-09-12.

Imaging: X-ray right knee, AP, lateral and tunnel views, on 2026-09-10. Result: small lucent area at the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle, possible osteochondritis dissecans, not confirmatory.

Physical examination (2026-09-26): Small effusion. Tenderness over the medial femoral condyle with the knee flexed. Positive Wilson test.

Physician rationale: Suspected osteochondritis dissecans; MRI needed to assess lesion stability and guide treatment.`,
};

const id = (String(query).toUpperCase().match(/CLM-\d+/) || [])[0];
if (!id) return 'No claim ID found in the request. Use the format CLM-####.';
if (!claims[id]) return 'Claim ' + id + ' not found. Known claims: ' + Object.keys(claims).join(', ');
return claims[id];

parameters.content:
## 1 · INGEST -- split the policy into chunks
Run once (and after every n8n restart). Loads MP-KNEE-08 into `medical_policy_mp08`. Claim files are read whole by get_claim_file, not searched.

## 2 · ASK -- AI drafts, human decides
Orchestrator agent → calls the MRI Reader sub-agent (reads the full claim file via get_claim_file), search_medical_policy (RAG over MP-KNEE-08), date_diff (exact day counts) and calculator. Output is a draft rationale with policy citations -- never a decision.
